title: Public and private keys
summary: Two halves of one key: lock for someone, and prove who signed a file.

scheme: ├── public key     give it to anyone
└── private key    only you have it
text: gpg -c locks a file with a passphrase you must share. Key pairs avoid that.
- The two halves are made together and work together.
- You can't compute the private key from the public one.
To send a secret to Sam, lock it with Sam's public key.
- Only Sam's private key opens it. Not even Ada can open it again.

scheme: you ── the vendor's public key ──▶ check
└── BAD signature: changed, or not theirs
text: It works the other way round for signatures.
- Only the vendor can sign; anyone with the public key can check.
- One byte changed in the file and the signature fails.
A signature is only as good as the public key you check it with.
- Get the key from the project's official site, or your distribution.
- Compare its fingerprint with the one the project publishes on its official site.
- A key found next to the download on a mirror proves nothing.
